mainTopic: Altar items whose איסור lapses once the fire takes hold, and the ברייתא about ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ and lenient and stringent impurities
overview: The amud opens by explaining why עולא had to teach that a קומץ caught by the altar fire counts as one unit, just like an אבר. רב אחאי draws a practical rule from this: a פיגול קומץ that is half on the מזבח and burning is brought up entirely. רבי יוחנן then rules that פיגול, נותר and טמא brought onto the מזבח lose their איסור. רב חסדא objects that the מזבח is not a מקוה, and רבי זירא limits the rule to where the fire has taken hold. רבי יצחק בר ביסנא challenges this from a ברייתא that says meat's טומאה can never leave it. רבא, רב פפא and רבינא each try to answer him. The גמרא then studies that ברייתא's proofs that ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ means a person's impurity, and explains רבי's proof from ״וְאָכַל״ through רב יצחק בר אבודימי. Finally it quotes a hard ברייתא about 'lenient' and 'stringent' cases and begins testing what they could mean. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the teaching about the handful was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that עולא had to say his rule about the קומץ, because we might have thought a separated handful is different from a connected limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that rule applies only to a limb, which is connected together. But a handful, which is made of separate bits, you might say it does not apply. So he teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why עולא's teaching about the קומץ is not obvious. We might have thought it only works for a solid אבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבר is one connected piece, so if the fire catches part of it, the whole thing clearly belongs to the מזבח. A קומץ is loose flour and oil, so we might have thought only the burning part counts. עולא teaches that the קומץ is also treated as one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: What might you have said: introduces a mistaken idea we could have had
A limb of an animal offering
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
He teaches us: the teaching is needed to rule out the mistake

phrases.english: What might you have said?
This applies only to a limb, which is connected;
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule that once the fire catches part of it, the whole thing goes back up on the מזבח.

phrases.english: but a handful, which is in separate pieces, say it does not;
so he teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous section, explaining why עולא's ruling about the קומץ was needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is not obvious by pointing out a possible mistaken distinction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A loose קומץ is not one unit, so only the part the fire caught would go back up
steps.terutzMaskana: A קומץ counts as one unit like an אבר

steps.title: A פיגול handful half on the ground and half on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי concludes that a קומץ of פיגול partly on the מזבח, with fire caught in it, is brought up entirely, even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי said: Therefore, a פיגול handful, half of which is lying on the ground and half of which was brought up onto the wood pile, if the fire took hold of it, I bring all of it up, even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי takes the idea that a קומץ is one unit and applies it to a practical case of a פיגול קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the קומץ is one unit, the fire catching the half on the altar makes the whole קומץ belong to the מזבח. So even the half still on the floor is brought up. This is allowed לכתחילה, not only after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
An offering made invalid by a wrong intention about the time of eating or burning
The arranged wood pile on the מזבח
The fire took hold of it
From the start; as the proper way to act

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'one unit' idea has a real practical result: the fire's hold on part of the קומץ makes all of it altar property.

phrases.english: Rav Achai said:
Therefore, this handful of piggul,
half of which lies on the ground
and half of which he brought up onto the wood pile,
and the fire took hold of it,
I bring all of it up, even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the 'one unit' rule in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פיגול קומץ partly caught by the fire on the מזבח is brought up entirely, even לכתחילה

steps.title: Disqualified items brought onto the altar lose their prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that פיגול, נותר and טמא brought up to the מזבח lose their איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: פיגול, נותר and impure meat that someone brought up to the altar lose their prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: once פיגול, נותר or טמא are brought onto the מזבח, their איסור goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three items are normally forbidden to eat and may be punished with כרת. רבי יוחנן says that being brought onto the מזבח cancels that איסור. The next steps will question how far this goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat left past its allowed time for eating
Ritually impure (here: impure sacrificial meat)
The prohibition has lapsed
The altar

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Piggul, notar, and impure meat
that someone brought up onto the altar,
their prohibition has left them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about disqualified items on the מזבח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול, נותר and טמא brought onto the מזבח lose their איסור

steps.title: Is the altar a purifying bath?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא is astonished: how could the מזבח remove impurity as if it were a מקוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Teacher of this! Is the altar a מקוה of purification?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with surprise. Simply putting something on the מזבח cannot make it pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity is removed by a מקוה, not by an altar. If simply bringing impure meat up to the מזבח removed its איסור, the מזבח would be acting like a מקוה. רב חסדא finds that unreasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of this (teaching)! An expression of astonishment
A ritual bath that purifies

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Teacher of this!
phrases.notes: He is calling out in amazement at whoever said this ruling.

phrases.english: Is the altar a purifying bath?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that bringing the items up to the מזבח removes their איסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מזבח is not a מקוה; just placing something there should not cancel its איסור

steps.title: Only once the fire has taken hold
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that רבי יוחנן means only where the altar fire has already caught the items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: He means where the fire took hold of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends רבי יוחנן by limiting the rule. It only applies once the fire has taken hold of the items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not simply being on the מזבח that removes the איסור. Once the fire has caught them, they have become the altar's 'food,' and so the איסור lapses. This answers רב חסדא, since the מזבח is not acting like a מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Where the fire took hold of them

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is where the fire took hold of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: שֶׁמָּשְׁלָה בָּהֶן הָאוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Merely bringing the items onto the מזבח removes their איסור
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור lapses only once the altar fire has taken hold of them
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי זירא, רבי יוחנן's rule works only after the fire catches the items, not by just placing them on the מזבח.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse about impurity that can leave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא cites a ברייתא that impure meat's טומאה can never leave it. That contradicts the idea that the fire removes its איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא objected: אחרים say: 'his impurity upon him' refers to one whose impurity can leave him. This excludes meat, whose impurity cannot leave it. But if רבי יוחנן is right, the meat's impurity does leave it through the fire!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר ביסנא brings a ברייתא to attack רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא says meat's טומאה can never leave it, but רבי יוחנן's rule seems to say the fire removes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'his impurity upon him' as talking about the person who eats, since a person can become pure in a מקוה. It excludes the meat, because meat's טומאה supposedly can never go away. If the altar fire can remove the meat's איסור, then meat's טומאה can also 'leave,' and the ברייתא's reasoning falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others say': an opinion quoted in a ברייתא
Impurity that departs; impurity that can be removed
And if it is so: if the statement under attack were true

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Bisna raised an objection:
Others say:
"Having his impurity upon him"
means one whose impurity can leave him;
this excludes meat,
whose impurity cannot leave it.
And if it is so,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי טוּמְאָה פּוֹרַחַת מִמֶּנּוּ עַל יְדֵי הָאוּר!
phrases.english: then its impurity does leave it, through the fire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule, even as limited by רבי זירא, from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the איסור of טמא meat lapses once the fire takes hold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes meat's טומאה can never leave it. If the fire removes it, that assumption is false.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'his impurity upon him' could be read as talking about the meat. The ברייתא reads them as talking about the person who eats.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא only means a מקוה cannot purify meat
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that when the ברייתא says the meat's טומאה never leaves, it only means it can't leave through a מקוה. It says nothing about the fire of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: we are talking about purifying it through a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer the question from the ברייתא. He narrows what the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said impure meat's טומאה can never leave it. רבא says this only means a מקוה won't help. So the fire of the מזבח could still take away its איסור, and רבי יוחנן's rule can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual bath used to become טהור
We are saying / we are talking about
By means of, through

phrases.english: Rava says:
We are speaking of purification through a ritual bath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עַל יְדֵי מִקְוֶה קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means impure meat can never lose its טומאה in any way at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means a מקוה cannot purify meat. The fire of the מזבח is a separate matter.

steps.title: The ברייתא never mentions a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's answer. The ברייתא doesn't mention a מקוה at all, so it can't be limited to one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the word 'מקוה' written there?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. The ברייתא speaks in general terms, so you can't say it is only about a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer depended on reading the ברייתא as being only about a מקוה. The ברייתא just says the טומאה never leaves, with no limits. So רבא's narrow reading doesn't fit the words.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it? (a word showing surprise or doubt)
It is written

phrases.english: Is 'ritual bath' written there?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's words never mention a מקוה, so they can't be limited to one.

steps.title: רב פפא: the ברייתא is about שלמים meat, which never goes on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא is about meat of a שלמים. That meat is eaten, not burned on the מזבח, so the מזבח can't remove its טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא says: we are dealing with meat of שלמים, which is not fit to be offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new answer to the question from step 6. He says the ברייתא is about a different kind of meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule only covers things that are fit to go up on the מזבח. The meat of a שלמים is meant to be eaten, not burned, so the מזבח does nothing for it. That is why the ברייתא can say its טומאה never leaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings; most of their meat is eaten
We are dealing with
Fit to be offered on the מזבח
Rather (brings a new answer after the last one was rejected)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa says:
We are dealing with the meat of peace offerings,
which is not fit for offering on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which case the source is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about all meat, including meat that goes on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about שלמים meat, which isn't fit for the מזבח. So it doesn't clash with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבינא: the verse is about something whose impurity leaves while it is whole
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reads ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ as speaking about something whose טומאה leaves while it is still whole. That rules out meat, whose טומאה only leaves once it is burned up and lessened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ means one whose טומאה can leave him while he is whole. That leaves out meat, whose טומאה does not leave while it is whole, only once it is lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives another answer. He reads the verse the ברייתא uses in a way that leaves meat out completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can become טהור while staying whole, by going to the מקוה. Meat only loses its איסור when the fire eats into it, so it is 'lacking' and not whole. So the verse, and the ברייתא based on it, isn't about meat at all, and רבי יוחנן's rule stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: "And his impurity is upon him" (ויקרא 7:20)
Flies away, departs
Whole, complete
Lacking, lessened
Is excluded, left out

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lacking' here means the meat has been partly eaten up by the fire on the מזבח. Only then does its איסור leave, as רבי זירא explained in step 5.

phrases.english: Ravina says:
"Having his impurity upon him" —
this is one whose impurity departs from him
while he is whole;
this excludes meat —

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין טוּמְאָה פּוֹרַחַת כְּשֶׁהוּא שָׁלֵם,
phrases.english: an item whose impurity does not depart while it is whole,
but only when it is lacking.
phrases.notes: In other words, once the fire has started to eat it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 6, different from רב פפא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verse so it doesn't cover meat at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse and the ברייתא are about impure meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is about something that becomes טהור while whole, like a person. Meat is left out, so there is no clash with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers were offered to the ברייתא. רבא said it only means a מקוה, and that was rejected. רב פפא said it is about שלמים meat that isn't fit for the מזבח. רבינא said the verse is only about something purified while whole.

steps.title: The ברייתא itself: the verse is about a person's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at the ברייתא itself. It says ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ is speaking about טומאת הגוף, an impure person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ — the verse is speaking about impurity of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא turns to study the ברייתא that was quoted earlier. This sets up the question and proof that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is about someone eating שלמים while impure. The ברייתא says the impurity mentioned there belongs to the person eating, not to the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (going back to look closely at a source quoted earlier)
Impurity of a person's body
The verse is speaking about

phrases.english: The matter itself:
"Having his impurity upon him" —
the verse speaks of impurity of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא that רבי יצחק בר ביסנא quoted in step 6 and looks at it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ is about an impure person eating the meat.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the meat's impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: how do we know the verse means the person's impurity? Maybe it means the meat's impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is about impurity of the body? Or maybe it is only about impurity of the meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible reading. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'his' in 'his impurity' could point back to the person or to the meat. The ברייתא wants a solid source that settles which one.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a challenge to the reading just given)
Or is it perhaps only
Impurity of the meat

phrases.english: Do you say it speaks of impurity of the body;
or is it only speaking of impurity of the meat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּטוּמְאַת הַגּוּף אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּטוּמְאַת בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose impurity does 'his impurity' mean: the person's or the meat's?

steps.title: Proof by comparing the same words in the verse about a person impure from a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves its reading with a גזירה שוה. Our verse says 'his impurity', and so does the verse about a person impure from a dead body. That verse is clearly about a person, so ours is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'his impurity', and there it says 'his impurity is upon him'. Just as there the verse is about impurity of the body, so too here it is about impurity of the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. It links our verse to another verse that uses the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר 19:13 the impurity clearly belongs to a person who touched a dead body. Because the same word is used in both places, the ברייתא reads ours the same way: it is about a person's body. This backs up step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here... and it says there (the opening of a גזירה שוה)
Learning one verse from another because they use the same word
Just as... so too

phrases.english: It is stated here: "his impurity,"
and it is stated there: "his impurity is upon him" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:13. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, matching the actual פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן בְּטוּמְאַת הַגּוּף הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: just as there the verse speaks of impurity of the body,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן בְּטוּמְאַת הַגּוּף הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.
phrases.english: so too here the verse speaks of impurity of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and proves the claim of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ is about an impure person, not impure meat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from במדבר 19:13, the verse about a person impure from a dead body.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns from a גזירה שוה with the verse about a person impure from a dead body that ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ means the person's impurity, not the meat's.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: plural sacrifices, singular impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי proves the verse is about an impure person because 'sacrifices' is plural while 'his impurity' is singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: since the sacrifices are mentioned in the plural and the impurity in the singular, the verse is speaking about the impurity of a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second proof, from רבי יוסי, that ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ means the person's impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls the offerings שלמים, which is plural. If 'his impurity' meant the meat's impurity, it should have been plural too. Because it is singular, it must refer to the single person who is eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural form
Singular form
Sacrifices, holy offerings

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Since the sacrifices are mentioned in the plural,
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 7:20 the offerings are called ״זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״, and שלמים is a plural word.

phrases.english: and the impurity is mentioned in the singular,
the verse is speaking of impurity of the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הוֹאִיל וְנֶאֶמְרוּ קָדָשִׁים בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof alongside the גזירה שוה of step 13.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The grammar of ויקרא 7:20: plural offerings, singular 'his'

steps.title: רבי: proof from the word 'and eat'
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the word ״וְאָכַל״ shows the verse is about an impure person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: from the word 'and eat' we see the verse is speaking about the impurity of a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a third proof, from רבי. He points to the word ״וְאָכַל״ but does not explain how it proves anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's proof is very short, and it is not obvious how one word proves the point. That is exactly why the גמרא will soon ask ״מַאי מַשְׁמַע״ about it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he eats,' a word from the next verse, ויקרא 7:21
Impurity of the body, meaning a person's impurity

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
"And eat": the verse is speaking of impurity of the body.
phrases.notes: ״וְאָכַל״ is in the next verse, ויקרא 7:21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof in the same ברייתא.

steps.title: אחרים: impurity that can leave
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say the verse speaks of something whose impurity can leave it, which is a person and not meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others said: 'his impurity is upon him' means someone whose impurity can go away. That leaves out meat, whose impurity never goes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings its last proof, from אחרים, based on the words 'upon him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the impurity is 'upon him' suggests it is there for now and could later leave. A person can become טהור again, but impure meat stays impure forever. So the verse must mean a person.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others,' a name for certain תנאים quoted without naming them
Literally 'flies away': goes away, leaves
This excludes, leaves out

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives several separate proofs that ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ עָלָיו״ is about an impure person: a גזירה שוה, רבי יוסי's plural/singular proof, רבי's ״וְאָכַל״, and אחרים's 'impurity that can leave'.

phrases.english: Others said:
"And his impurity is upon him":
this means one whose impurity can leave him;
this excludes meat,
since impurity does not leave it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final proof of the ברייתא, ending the quote.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'upon him' imply impurity that can be removed

steps.title: How does 'and eat' prove it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי's proof and asks how the word ״וְאָכַל״ shows the verse is about a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי says 'and eat' shows the verse speaks of a person's impurity. How is that implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי's short proof and asks how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְאָכַל״ is in a different verse (7:21), and that verse is already clearly about a person. It is not clear how a word there tells us what 'his impurity' means in 7:20.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this implied? Where do we see it?

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi says: "and eat":
the verse is speaking of impurity of the body.
From where is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי's proof (step 15) to clarify it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word ״וְאָכַל״ proves that the verse refers to טומאת הגוף

steps.title: רבא praises two great explainers
steps.stepSummary: רבא says no one could explain verses like רב יצחק בר אבודימי, or ברייתות like זעירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: any verse that רב יצחק בר אבודימי did not explain, and any ברייתא that זעירי did not explain, remains unexplained.
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא brings רבא's praise of two scholars. This sets up the answer to רבי's proof in the next step, and also the ברייתא that זעירי explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is saying that רבי's hard proof can only be understood through רב יצחק בר אבודימי. His mention of זעירי prepares for the difficult ברייתא the גמרא quotes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse
Here: a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
It is not explained, it stays unclear

phrases.english: Rava said:
Any verse that was not explained by
Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל מַתְנִיתָא דְּלָא מְפָרֵשׁא לַהּ (רַב) זְעֵירִי –
phrases.english: and any baraita that was not explained by (Rav) Ze'eiri,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets and just say זעירי.

phrases.english: is not explained.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כׇּל קְרָא דְּלָא מְפָרֵשׁ לֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the authority whose explanation will answer step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Verses are best explained by רב יצחק בר אבודימי, and ברייתות by זעירי.

steps.title: Feminine, masculine, feminine
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבודימי explains: like the next verse, our verse starts and ends in feminine form with a masculine word in the middle, and it still speaks of the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רב יצחק בר אבודימי said: since the verse begins in the feminine and ends in the feminine, with the masculine in the middle, the verse is speaking of a person's impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how ״וְאָכַל״ proves רבי's point, using רב יצחק בר אבודימי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 7:21 the verse opens and closes with feminine words about the נפש, yet ״וְאָכַל״ in the middle is masculine, and it clearly means the person. Verse 7:20 has the same pattern, so its masculine ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ״ also means the person, not the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Feminine form
Masculine form
In the middle

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the masculine word must refer to the masculine word בשר. רבי's point is that the Torah sometimes switches to masculine when it is still talking about the person, as ״וְאָכַל״ shows.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי:
phrases.english: This is what Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi said:
Since the verse begins in the feminine form
phrases.notes: In 7:21: ״וְנֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִגַּע״ starts it, and ״וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ״ ends it. Both are feminine.

phrases.english: and ends in the feminine form,
with the masculine form in the middle,
the verse is speaking of impurity of the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי: הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח הַכָּתוּב בִּלְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the explanation promised by רבא's praise.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 7:21 switches to masculine (״וְאָכַל״) in the middle and still means the person, so the masculine ״וְטֻמְאָתוֹ״ in 7:20's same pattern also means the person.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a change of grammatical gender in a verse does not automatically mean the subject has changed.

steps.title: The hard ברייתא: why both lenient and stringent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that זעירי explained. It asks why the Torah states both 'lenient' and 'stringent' cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא, as it was taught: if the lenient ones were stated, why were the stringent ones stated? And if the stringent ones were stated, why were the lenient ones stated?
steps.whatsHappening: Having mentioned זעירי, the גמרא now quotes the ברייתא he explained. This step sets up the ברייתא's own question, and its answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the Torah wrote about both 'lenient' and 'stringent' cases and asks why each is needed. It does not say what these cases are, and that is why it needs זעירי's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Lenient ones, less severe cases
Stringent ones, more severe cases

phrases.english: The baraita, as it was taught:
If the lenient ones were stated,
why were the stringent ones stated,
and if the stringent ones were stated,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the round-bracket word; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The same goes for the rest of this ברייתא.

phrases.english: why were the lenient ones stated?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתָא – דְּתַנְיָא: אִם נֶאֶמְרוּ קַלּוֹת לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ חֲמוּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up the second half of רבא's statement, about זעירי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברייתא asks why the Torah needs to state both lenient and stringent cases.

steps.title: Why each set had to be written
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that each set of cases teaches something the other could not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only the lenient were stated, I would say the lenient carry a לאו and the stringent carry death, so the stringent were stated. If only the stringent were stated, I would say one is liable only for the stringent and exempt for the lenient, so the lenient were stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question by showing the mistake we would make if either set were missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the lenient written, we would give the stringent a harsher punishment (מיתה), so the Torah writes the stringent to show they are equal. With only the stringent written, we would think the lenient are completely exempt, so the Torah writes them too. The ברייתא still does not say which cases are 'lenient' and 'stringent', so זעירי's explanation is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment, here punished with lashes
Death, here meaning death at the hands of Heaven
I would have said: what we would wrongly think otherwise
Exempt, not punished

phrases.english: If the lenient were stated and not the stringent,
I would have said:
for the lenient, one is punished for a prohibition,
and for the stringent, with death;
therefore the stringent were stated.
And if the stringent were stated and the lenient were not stated,
I would have said:
for the stringent one is liable,
and for the lenient one is exempt;
therefore the lenient were stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נֶאֶמְרוּ קַלּוֹת וְלֹא חֲמוּרוֹת – הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא answers the question it asked in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each set prevents a mistake: without the stringent we would punish them more harshly, and without the lenient we would exempt them entirely.

steps.title: What are the lenient and stringent cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'lenient' and 'stringent.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the 'lenient' cases, and what are the 'stringent' cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly the ברייתא means by 'lenient' and 'stringent.' This question sets up the attempts to answer it that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke about lenient and stringent cases but never said which cases it meant. Until we know, we cannot follow its reasoning. So the גמרא will try out possible answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The lenient cases
The stringent cases

phrases.english: What are the lenient ones, and what are the stringent ones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the terms in the ברייתא from Steps 20–21 refer to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which cases the ברייתא calls 'lenient' and which it calls 'stringent.'

steps.title: Suggesting מעשר and תרומה, and rejecting it
steps.stepSummary: A first suggestion: the lenient case is מעשר and the stringent case is תרומה. It is rejected because תרומה really is punished with death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the lenient case is מעשר and the stringent case is תרומה, how could the ברייתא say 'I would have thought it is punished with death'? Even now, that really is the law: it is punished with death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the lenient case is מעשר and the stringent case is תרומה. It immediately rejects this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke as if thinking the stringent case carries מיתה would be a mistake. But a טמא person who eats תרומה really is punished with מיתה at the hands of Heaven. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be tested)
מעשר שני, the second tithe
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Punished with death at the hands of Heaven

phrases.english: If you say the lenient case is מעשר,
and the stringent case is תרומה,
how can it say 'I would have said it is punished with death'?!
Even now, it really is punished with death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a first answer to Step 22 and knocks it down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the stringent case is תרומה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Eating תרומה while טמא really does carry מיתה, so calling that a mistaken thought makes no sense.

steps.title: A second problem: a קל וחומר cannot go beyond its source
steps.stepSummary: A second argument against מעשר/תרומה: a קל וחומר from מעשר could never have produced a death penalty, because of דיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, how can it say, 'If they had not been stated, I would have said it is punished with death'? It is enough for what is learned from a קל וחומר to be like its source!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason why the lenient case cannot be מעשר and the stringent case cannot be תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only מעשר had been written, we would learn about תרומה through a קל וחומר. But the rule of דיו לבא מן הדין says the result can be no harsher than its source. מעשר only carries lashes, so the קל וחומר could never have given us a death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another problem)

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: What is learned through a קל וחומר is no stricter than its source

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean תרומה is free of מיתה. The point is only that a קל וחומר could never have taught us מיתה, so the ברייתא's 'I would have said' does not fit.

phrases.english: And furthermore: 'And if they had not been stated,'
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: 'I would have said it is punished with death'?!
It is enough for what comes from a קל וחומר
to be like its source!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, וְאִי לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר בְּמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the same suggestion.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as מעשר (lenient) and תרומה (stringent).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of דיו, a קל וחומר from מעשר could never yield מיתה, so the ברייתא's 'I would have said death' is impossible.

steps.title: A new suggestion: טומאת שרץ and טומאת מת
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the lenient case is טומאת שרץ and the stringent case is טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the lenient case is the טומאה of a שרץ, and the stringent case is the טומאה of a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer. Lenient and stringent describe two kinds of טומאה the person has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the difference is not between foods but between kinds of טומאה. טומאת שרץ is the lighter kind and טומאת מת is the heavier kind. The next step will test this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switching to a new answer)
טומאה from touching a dead creeping creature
טומאה from a dead human body

phrases.english: Rather, the lenient case is the טומאה of a שרץ,
and the stringent case is the טומאה of a dead body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected מעשר/תרומה suggestion with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lenient means טומאת שרץ, and stringent means טומאת מת.

steps.title: Which food? If it is תרומה, both carry death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which food this is about. If it is תרומה, both kinds of טומאה carry מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about which food is this? If it is about תרומה, both this one and that one are punished with death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new answer by asking which food the person is eating. It shows that תרומה does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומה, it makes no difference what kind of טומאה the person has. Whether it came from a שרץ or from a מת, eating תרומה while טמא carries מיתה. So there is no lenient or stringent difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And about what? (which food)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: And about what food? If it is about תרומה,
both this one and that one are punished with death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the שרץ/מת answer if the food is תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The שרץ/מת reading, applied to תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For תרומה, both kinds of טומאה carry the same death penalty, so there is no lenient versus stringent case.

steps.title: Furthermore: תרומה is not just a לאו
steps.stepSummary: A second problem with תרומה: the ברייתא says the stringent case teaches it is only a לאו, but תרומה carries death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, how can it say, 'This is why the stringent cases were stated: to teach that it is only a לאו'? It is punished with death! (And how can it say, 'If they had not been stated, I would have said death'? It is enough for what comes from a קל וחומר to be like its source!)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another reason the שרץ/מת answer cannot be about תרומה. Some versions also repeat the דיו argument here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the stringent case was written to teach that it carries only a לאו, meaning lashes. But eating תרומה while טמא carries מיתה, so it cannot be 'only a לאו.' The words in brackets repeat the דיו problem from Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: This is why they were stated
Only a prohibition, punished with lashes

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's lenient and stringent cases cannot involve תרומה, because eating תרומה while טמא is always punished with מיתה. The גמרא must find a different food.

phrases.english: And furthermore: 'This is why the stringent cases were stated, to teach it is a לאו'?!
It is punished with death!
(And: 'if they had not been stated,'
phrases.notes: This whole sentence is in round brackets, so some versions leave it out. It repeats the argument from Step 24.

phrases.english: 'I would have said it is punished with death'?!
It is enough for what comes from a קל וחומר
to be like its source!)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to applying the שרץ/מת reading to תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the stringent case teaches 'only a לאו,' if the food is תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating תרומה while טמא carries מיתה, so it cannot be described as only a לאו.

steps.title: Testing the second option: eating מעשר
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting תרומה, the גמרא turns to the other choice, eating מעשר, and opens a new difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the ברייתא is talking about eating מעשר (this is also hard).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It is about to show that the other possible food, מעשר, also causes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא asked which food the ברייתא means and gave two choices. Steps 26 and 27 knocked out תרומה. This line moves to the second choice, מעשר. The actual problem with מעשר will be spelled out in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: And if (opens the second option)
Eating מעשר (the tithe) while טמא

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full question yet. It only names the second option. The real difficulty comes in the next line.

phrases.english: And if it is about eating מעשר,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 26 and 27 rejected תרומה, this step opens the second option from step 26, eating מעשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 25 that the light case is טומאת שרץ and the strict case is טומאת מת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible foods have to fail for the answer to fall. תרומה already failed, so now the גמרא tests מעשר. The details come in the next line.
